newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo mayor's assets seized in bond scam probe.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo mayor's assets seized in bond scam probe.

text.p: A court has seized $750,000 in assets of Sao Paulo Mayor Celso Pitta, one of dozens of high-level officials under investigation in an alleged multimillion-dollar bond scam, a prosecutor said on Thursday.
"This is a precautionary measure to guarantee reimbursement" for any losses to the city, said Sao Paulo prosecutor Wallace Martins.
Among Pitta's assets were apartments in Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro and four cars, Martins said.
Congressional investigators charge that dozens of high- level state and city officials across Brazil rigged municipal and state bond auctions to benefit a select group of banks.
Pitta, mayor of Brazil's and South America's largest city, is the most powerful official linked to the scam.
Although he has not been tied directly to the fraud, Pitta did serve as the city's finance chief when the bond auctions were carried out.
The embattled mayor has continually denied any wrongdoing and said he would appeal the court's decision to seize his assets.
